title: Observation Bridge: non-intrusive traffic observation proxy with per-tenant sampling and credit fences
creator: Priya Kapoor
description:
Problem: We need a safe, low-risk mechanism to run production traffic through alternate evaluation paths (canary variants, A/B backends, offline evaluators) without affecting customer-facing latency or billing. Existing shadow/mirroring work is mature but many tickets are tightly coupled to replication semantics. This ticket proposes an Observation Bridge: a read-only, non-blocking proxy at the edge/gateway that can duplicate a configurable subset of requests to sandboxed downstream consumers while enforcing strict cost and tenant isolation policies.

Goals:
- Observe production traffic with zero blocking of the primary response path and bounded additional cost.
- Per-tenant adaptive sampling driven by credit pools and behavioral budgets.
- Strong isolation: duplicates must never impact live throughput, token accounting, or KV cache population used by serving runtime.
- Easy operator controls (sampling policies, budgets, emergency quiesce) surfaced in Console and via HTTP admin API.
- Integrate with rollout workflows: canary A/B cohorts, regression detectors, and auto-rollback triggers.

Design notes / approach:
1) Read-only edge hook: implement a lightweight module in the gateway that creates a duplicate event object for observed requests. The module will be careful to: strip sensitive headers/PII via a configurable scrubber, remove or redact user identifiers unless explicitly allowed, and mark duplicates as "sandboxed" so downstream consumers opt out of influencing production state.
2) Async fanout: duplicates are enqueued to an internal async pipeline (kafka-like stream or internal queue) and processed by dedicated Observation Workers. This guarantees 0ms added latency on the primary response.
3) Sampling controller: a centralized service evaluates per-tenant policies and returns sampling decisions. Policies include static rate, decaying reservoir (for gradual onboarding), and credit-based budgets that are deducted as duplicates are executed. Tenants with exhausted credits are automatically quarantined from duplication.
4) Cost fence & accounting: duplicates are executed in a separate chargeback accounting system. Duplicate consumption is billed to a sandbox bucket and tracked in Console for visibility. Auto-throttle when daily duplicate spend for org > X% of allowed budget.
5) Sandbox runtime flags: workers run variants in sandboxes that disable KV cache writes, do not emit production traces unless requested, and cannot write to external data sinks except audit logs.
6) Circuit breakers & safe default: if Observation Workers lag > 5x baseline or duplicate error rate > 5% for 1 minute, auto-disable duplication for affected tenants and raise high-priority alert.

Implementation plan (high level):
- Phase A (MVP): implement gateway hook + queue + simple worker that forwards duplicates to a separate endpoint (canary cluster or evaluation lambda). Basic sampling controller with static rates and tenant global cap. Console toggles for per-route sampling.
- Phase B: add credit-based budgets, tenant quarantine, per-tenant reporting in Console, header scrubbing rules, and basic auto-throttle.
- Phase C: full integration with rollout pipelines: route-level canary cohorts, automatic discrepancy detectors (logit/embedding drift checks), and auto-rollback hooks that can flip a rollout flag if regressions exceed thresholds.

Open design trade-offs we need to document and decide:
- Queue semantics: durable (kafka) vs in-memory (kinesis-like) for lower latency and simpler ops. Durable gives replay but increases operational complexity.
- Level of redaction for PII-sensitive customers: default scrub vs allowlist per-tenant.
- How strictly to decouple KV cache: we must ensure duplicates never warm production caches, but this needs runtime changes (sdk/headers).

Deliverables / artifacts:
- RFC describing API between gateway and sampling controller (Confluence draft).
- Gateway module PR and unit tests.
- Observation Worker service + integration tests and load harness.
- Console controls and per-tenant metrics dashboards.
- Regression detector prototype and auto-rollback hook.

Acceptance criteria:
acceptance_criteria: Gateway duplication adds < 1ms p50 latency overhead to primary request path
Sandboxed duplicates cannot write to production KV cache or mutate persistent state
Per-tenant sampling policy respects credit budgets and prevents overrun beyond configured threshold
Console shows per-route duplicate spend and allows immediate quiesce of duplication for any tenant
Auto-throttle triggers when duplicate processing lag > 5x baseline and successfully disables duplication for affected tenants
tasks: Write RFC for Observation Bridge and sampling controller (Confluence)
Implement gateway hook with scrubber and enqueue semantics
Build Sampling Controller service with static and credit-based policies
Create Observation Worker skeleton and sandbox runtime flags
Add metrics and billing instrumentation (duplicate tokens, worker lag, error rates)
Console UI for per-route duplication controls and spend dashboards
Integrate auto-throttle and circuit-breaker logic with alerting
End-to-end load tests and chaos test (simulate worker lag/exhausted credits)
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Duplicate traffic accidentally affects production caches or billing. Mitigation: enforce sandbox flag at runtime and add unit tests that assert no KV writes from sandboxed context; billing pipeline tags duplicates before processing.
Risk: High duplicate traffic spikes cost. Mitigation: credit fences with emergency quiesce and default conservative sampling rates; operator override in Console.
Risk: Operational complexity if durable queue chosen. Mitigation: start with managed streaming service for MVP and evaluate cost/ops after Phase A.
monitoring_and_alerting: Metric: duplicate.worker.lag (per-tenant and global) with P95 and max alarms
Dashboard: per-route duplicate spend and token counts
Alert: auto-quiesce invoked with affected tenant list and correlation id
rollout_plan: Step 0: Deploy gateway hook disabled by default in staging
Step 1: Enable Observation Bridge for internal dev tenants at 5% sampling
Step 2: Gradually onboard 3 low-risk customers (10% -> 25%) with monitoring
Step 3: Open to all customers behind conservative defaults and credit opt-in
Auto-rollback triggers: p99 latency increase > 10% OR route error-rate increase > 2% attributable to duplication
testing_plan: Unit tests for gateway hook and scrubber rules
Integration tests where duplicate path is exercised but primary path remains unchanged
Load test with synthetic traffic that simulates token-heavy and short requests to validate cost fences
Chaos test: simulate worker downtime and ensure circuit-breaker disables duplication without impacting primary path
Privacy test: verify redaction rules for a sample of high-sensitivity tenants
